title: Predictive Prefetch Orchestrator — Design & Validation
author: Sasha Nguyen
content:
Summary
-------
This document defines the Predictive Prefetch Orchestrator (PPO): a runtime component that predicts future token or KV-cache accesses and prefetches required KV pages / model artifacts into local memory or a warm cache tier. The goal is to reduce tail latency and cold-KV misses while preserving cost and fidelity SLOs. It describes architecture, scheduling interactions, configuration, validation tests, rollout plan, and incident runbooks.

Scope and goals
----------------
- Primary goal: reduce 99th/99.9th percentile token latency for long-context and multi-turn workloads by reducing on-path cache-miss stalls.
- Secondary goals: keep incremental cost per useful token < 6% of baseline; avoid fidelity regressions and avoid noisy eviction patterns that increase GPU OOM risk.
- Out of scope: model quantization decisions, model selection routing. PPO only orchestrates prefetch hints and local memory priming.

High-level architecture
-----------------------
Components (logical):
1) Predictor service (stateless microservice): serves a lightweight sequence predictor that emits prefetch hints per request. Implements a rate limit and confidence score.
2) Prefetch coordinator (in-runtime agent): receives hints, applies admission control, schedules prefetch work to worker threads or a background prefetch pool.
3) KV-cache manager (existing component): accepts explicit prefetch requests (page ids) and reports outcomes (hit, miss, duration).
4) Observability adapter: enriches traces with prefetch provenance and metrics (prefetch_count, prefetch_success, prefetch_cost_us).
5) Admission controller and scheduler hook: integrates with kernel scheduler to avoid prefetch storms and respects SLO-driven credit accounting.

Data flow (textual diagram):
- API request -> request classifier -> predictor service (async call) -> emits N prefetch hints (page_id, score, lookahead_ms) -> prefetch coordinator applies policy -> enqueues prefetch -> KV-cache manager fetches/warms pages -> request proceeds using possibly warmed KV/cache.

Predictor model and signals
---------------------------
- Predictor is intentionally small (few hundred KB parameters) to keep inference cheap and fast. It operates in two modes: deterministic rule-based (fallback) and statistical scoring (ML).
- Features used: session token histogram, user agent, route, model variant, recent completion lengths, last-k page access sequence, request timestamp, and cohort id.
- Labels for training: subsequent page access within lookahead window (e.g., 200ms) derived from production traces (shadow mode).
- Retraining cadence: weekly for high-change routes; monthly for stable routes.

Admission control & scheduler integration
-----------------------------------------
Admission policy is the safety layer that prevents prefetch work from interfering with on-path kernels. Key levers:
- Prefetch budget per-GPU per-second (pages/sec). Default: 50 pages/sec per GPU.
- Prefetch priority class: BACKGROUND_LOW, BACKGROUND_HIGH. Background_low is throttled under any kernel contention.
- Kernel credit check: prefetch pool only consumes credits from a separate prefetch bucket; if runtime kernel load > 70% or tail latency SLO is threatened, prefetches are suspended.

Configuration table (recommended defaults)
-----------------------------------------
| key | default | description |
| prefetch.enabled | true | master switch |
| prefetch.lookahead_ms | 200 | max lookahead window to consider access relevant |
| prefetch.max_pages_per_request | 6 | cap per prediction |
| prefetch.gpu_budget_pages_per_sec | 50 | budget enforced by admission controller |
| prefetch.min_score_threshold | 0.55 | predictor confidence cutoff |
| prefetch.priority_mode | BACKGROUND_LOW | default priority class |
| prefetch.shadow_mode | true | if true, metrics are collected but prefetches aren't applied to on-path traffic |

Example runtime YAML config
---------------------------
```yaml
prefetch:
  enabled: true
  lookahead_ms: 200
  max_pages_per_request: 4
  gpu_budget_pages_per_sec: 50
  min_score_threshold: 0.6
  priority_mode: BACKGROUND_HIGH
  shadow_mode: false
```

Observability & KPIs
--------------------
Minimum dashboards (per-cluster and per-route):
- Prefetch hit rate (prefetch_success / prefetch_attempts) — target > 70% for routes with high sequentiality.
- Delta tail latency (p99, p999) before vs after prefetch action — target p99 reduction >= 10ms for targeted routes.
- Prefetch-induced kernel wait time — should be < 1% of total kernel time.
- Cost delta per-useful-token — target < +6%.
- False-positive prefetch ratio (pages prefetched but not accessed in lookahead) — target < 30% for production routes.

Metric naming suggestions:
- runtime.prefetch.attempts
- runtime.prefetch.success
- runtime.prefetch.latency_ms
- runtime.prefetch.evictions_caused
- runtime.prefetch.cpu_time_ms
- runtime.prefetch.provenance (predictor_rule/modelid)

Validation and testing strategy
-------------------------------
1) Offline validation: train predictor on historical shadow traces and compute precision/recall w.r.t. lookahead windows. Generate cohort-level charts (by route/model/sequence-length).
2) Synthetic replay: use the operational workload simulator to replay requests and run PPO in shadow mode. Collect metrics: predicted pages, accessed pages, cost.
3) Shadow-canary: enable shadow_mode=false only for a small set of pods (5% traffic) but with prefetch priority = BACKGROUND_LOW and fast rollback toggle. Monitor KPIs for 48h.
4) Canary with adaptive throttle: increase active prefetch traffic to 20% and enable dynamic budget. Continue validation for 7 days and run A/B analysis for latency and cost.

Shadow experiment commands (examples)
------------------------------------
- Toggle shadow mode (kubectl):
  kubectl patch deployment/runtime-pool -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"runtime.prefs.prefetch-shadow":"true"}}}}}'
- Query prefetch metrics (promql):
  sum(rate(runtime_prefetch_attempts_total[5m])) by (cluster, route)
  sum(rate(runtime_prefetch_success_total[5m])) / sum(rate(runtime_prefetch_attempts_total[5m]))

Rollout checklist
------------------
1) Offline precision >= 0.65 and recall >= 0.35 for target routes.
2) Shadow-mode pilot: prefetch_success >= 50% and false_positive <= 40%.
3) Canary: no >25% regression in p99SLO and prefetch_cost_delta within budget for 48h.
4) Gradual ramp: 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with 24–72h stabilization windows and automated rollback on SLA breaches.

Safety & fallback patterns
-------------------------
- Automatic suspend: if runtime.p99_latency increases by >10% over 15m or prefetch_eviction_events > threshold, suspend prefetch globally and notify oncall.
- Degraded planner: switch predictor to deterministic rule-based prefetch (e.g., last-2-pages prefetch) if model confidence drops.
- Eviction-aware prefetch: track prefetch-caused evictions and deprioritize prefetches that historically caused cross-tenant memory pressure.

Incident runbook (cache-thrash loop)
------------------------------------
Trigger: sudden spike in cache evictions correlated with prefetch.activity and rising p99 latency.
1) Pager routes to PPO-oncall.
2) Run quick inspection: check metrics
   - pref_attempts = curl "http://metrics/api?query=rate(runtime_prefetch_attempts_total[5m])"
   - evictions = curl "http://metrics/api?query=rate(runtime_prefetch_evictions_total[5m])"
3) If evictions / attempts > 0.2 and p99 latency > SLO, execute emergency suspend:
   curl -XPOST http://runtime-admin/api/prefetch/suspend
4) If suspend is successful, monitor p99 for 10m. If stable, adjust GPU budget down (e.g., -50%) and re-enable with BACKGROUND_LOW.
5) Postmortem steps: collect traces, predictor inputs, and candidate root causes (miscalibrated score, dataset shift, route misclassification).

Operational playbooks and experiments
------------------------------------
- Periodic prefetch audit (weekly): run the Audit Script (see below) to estimate wasted pages and correlation with evictions.
- Controlled stress test: synthetic-burst profile to measure prefetch behavior under admission constraints.
- KPI drift detector: daily job that surfaces routes with falling prefetch precision or rising false positives.

Audit script (pseudo-CLI)
-------------------------
# Download 24h shadow traces for route X and compute metrics
redwood traces extract --route X --since 24h | redwood prefetch-audit --lookahead 200 --output /tmp/audit.json
redwood prefetch-audit-report /tmp/audit.json --format html --out /tmp/prefetch-audit-routeX.html

Developer guidelines for contributors
------------------------------------
- Prefer simple predictors and keep feature sets stable for production routes.
- Annotate predictor versions in metric provenance (predictor:v2).
- Add unit tests for admission controller thresholds and an end-to-end shadow-mode integration test.
- Keep retraining dataset windows (e.g., last 14 days) configurable per-route.

Appendix: small example of prefetch hint JSON
--------------------------------------------
{
  "request_id": "abcd-1234",
  "route": "/chat/gpt-extended",
  "hints": [
    {"page_id": "kv:mdl:1234:page:42", "score": 0.78, "lookahead_ms": 180},
    {"page_id": "kv:mdl:1234:page:43", "score": 0.61, "lookahead_ms": 180}
  ],
  "predictor_version": "v2025-09-03",
  "timestamp": "2025-11-20T16:23:04Z"
}
Notes and migration considerations
---------------------------------
- Start with read-heavy routes and long-context chat routes that have high sequential locality. Avoid bursty short-completion routes for early pilots.
- Coordinate with kernel-scheduler owners to add the prefetch priority class to the scheduling credit model.
- Expected incremental infra cost: small CPU overhead for predictor service + network egress to KV tier. Estimate: ~0.5–2% increase in infra cost for routes where prefetch is enabled.
